name: Inman Park
tagline: Victorian & Craftsman Due Diligence Audits in Atlanta's First Planned Suburb
intro: Inman Park is renowned for its grand Queen Anne Victorians, ornate Craftsman bungalows, and tree-lined corridors along the Atlanta BeltLine. While these architectural gems hold tremendous character, purchasing in Inman Park requires specialized diagnostic evaluation of century-old construction systems, early-century additions, and historic district overlay constraints.

keyDefects.title: Knob-and-Tube Wiring & Mixed Electrical Eras
keyDefects.description: Many historic Inman Park homes still retain active or abandoned knob-and-tube branch wiring buried beneath attic insulation or concealed behind original plaster walls. Our dual-inspector team uses non-destructive electrical circuit tracers and thermal imaging to identify ungrounded circuits and overloaded subpanels.

keyDefects.title: Granite & Brick Pier Foundation Settlement
keyDefects.description: Original stone and brick pier foundations common in early 1900s Victorians are vulnerable to mortar deterioration, unlevel beam settling, and inadequate crawlspace ventilation. We perform laser-level elevation scans and joist deflection assessments.

keyDefects.title: Cast Iron Plumbing & Clay Sewer Laterals
keyDefects.description: 100-year-old subterranean sewer connections in Inman Park frequently suffer from tree root intrusion, internal pipe scaling, and channel bellies. A high-definition fiber-optic sewer scope is essential before closing.

keyDefects.title: Plaster & Lath Wall Moisture Traps
keyDefects.description: Dense lath-and-plaster walls can mask slow roof and chimney leaks. Our FLIR infrared thermal cameras scan wall cavities to pinpoint hidden moisture intrusion behind vintage trim and historic chimneys.

faqs.question: What are the most common inspection findings in Inman Park historic homes?
faqs.answer: The most frequent issues in Inman Park include active or dormant knob-and-tube wiring, deteriorating cast iron drain lines, crawlspace joist sag from historic moisture, and ungrounded three-prong electrical outlets installed during unpermitted past renovations.

faqs.question: Does Foresight inspect homes with historic preservation restrictions?
faqs.answer: Yes. Christopher Boykin, CMI, and our team are thoroughly experienced with Inman Park Historic District guidelines, helping buyers understand what modifications require Urban Design Commission (UDC) approval versus standard maintenance repairs.

faqs.question: Why is a sewer scope inspection critical in Inman Park?
faqs.answer: Inman Park's mature canopy of oak and pecan trees creates significant root pressure on original vitrified clay and cast iron sewer laterals connecting to the City of Atlanta main line. Our 200ft camera inspection identifies bellies, fractures, and blockages before you finalize your purchase.

faqs.question: How long does a dual-inspector historic audit take in Inman Park?
faqs.answer: Due to our two-inspector protocol, a complex 3,500 sq ft Victorian is typically completed in 2.0 to 2.5 hours, providing double the technical oversight in half the time of a solo inspector.
